seed_papers.title: Hybrid Retrieval Architecture with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
seed_papers.text:
Abstract
We evaluate a hybrid retrieval system that merges dense vector inner-product search with sparse BM25 lexical scoring using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with constant k=60.

Methodology
Each document is partitioned into section-aware segments using a sliding window overlap of 64 tokens. Embeddings are computed with a 384-dimensional local encoder.

Results
On the SciFact and HotpotQA benchmarks, hybrid RRF improves top-5 recall by 14.2 percent compared to dense-only search while adding less than 8 milliseconds of CPU overhead.

Limitations
Extremely long mathematical tables with sparse prose can still degrade tokenization accuracy.

seed_papers.title: Grammar-Constrained Planning for Small Quantized Language Models
seed_papers.text:
Abstract
Small language models between 1.5B and 3B parameters often fail during unconstrained multi-turn tool calling. We introduce a single-shot Plan-then-Execute architecture enforced via GBNF context-free grammars.

Methodology
The planner generates an execution plan capped at 4 deterministic tool steps validated by Pydantic schemas before any external tool runs. Model weights are quantized to 4-bit Q4_K_M GGUF format.

Results
Across 500 tool-use tasks on a 2-vCPU processor, GBNF grammar enforcement increases JSON schema validity from 61.4 percent to 100.0 percent and cuts retry latency by 47 percent.

Limitations
Fixed plans cannot dynamically invent new tool definitions mid-execution.

seed_papers.title: Sandboxed XML Contexts Against Indirect PDF Prompt Injection
seed_papers.text:
Abstract
Academic PDFs harvested from open repositories represent an untrusted input vector capable of indirect prompt injection via microscopic or white-colored font spans.

Methodology
Our parser discards PDF text spans with font size below 2.0 points or hexadecimal color 0xFFFFFF. Remaining chunks are wrapped in untrusted_paper_content XML tags and verified by a regex citation validator.

Results
In adversarial red-team evaluations covering 250 poisoned PDFs, span filtering plus XML sandboxing blocked 99.2 percent of instruction-override attacks and eliminated unauthorized external markdown links.

Limitations
Obfuscated payloads embedded inside rasterized figures require OCR inspection.

seed_papers.title: Map-Reduce Literature Matrix Synthesis with Verifiable Citations
seed_papers.text:
Abstract
Concatenating multiple full-length research papers into a single context window causes severe cross-paper attribution errors in sub-3B parameter models.

Methodology
We decompose literature review generation into an independent per-paper Map phase extracting problem, methodology, benchmarks, and primary_chunk_id, followed by a deterministic Python Reduce phase that compiles the Markdown table.

Results
Evaluated on 120 multi-paper synthesis tasks, Map-Reduce lowers cross-paper citation swaps from 28.5 percent down to 1.1 percent while fitting comfortably inside a 4096-token context window.

Limitations
Per-paper sequential mapping scales linearly with the number of compared papers.

seed_papers.title: Cost-Zero Serverless Persistence for Ephemeral AI Workloads
seed_papers.text:
Abstract
Containerized AI applications hosted on ephemeral CPU instances lose local vector indices upon container sleep or restart. We design a zero-cost persistence layer within strict cloud free-tier quotas.

Methodology
Parsed papers are stored as single gzip-compressed JSON bundles in S3 to stay under the 2000 monthly PUT limit, while session state and 24-hour query caches reside in a single-table DynamoDB store provisioned at 5 RCU and 5 WCU.

Results
Cold-start index hydration from S3 completes in 1.8 seconds for 10000 chunks, and DynamoDB query caching reduces duplicate CPU inference load by 63 percent.

Limitations
Provisioned capacity of 5 WCU requires batching during large bulk backfills.

seed_papers.title: Calibrated Abstention Gates for Citation-Grounded Question Answering
seed_papers.text:
Abstract
Question answering assistants must abstain when retrieved evidence does not support a verifiable answer rather than speculating from parametric memory.

Methodology
We compute a calibrated hybrid confidence score combining 55 percent dense cosine similarity, 35 percent normalized BM25 score, and 10 percent RRF rank agreement, enforcing a refusal threshold of 0.32.

Results
On out-of-domain and unanswerable probes, the 0.32 confidence gate achieves a 96.8 percent true abstention rate while maintaining 94.5 percent answer coverage on in-domain questions.

Limitations
Highly abbreviated acronym queries may require query expansion to pass the lexical component.
